entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-m65p-9j7q-6w33: MLflow vulnerable to arbitrary file read on unauthenticated servers via prompt model version source
entry.content:
MLflow vulnerable to arbitrary file read on unauthenticated servers via prompt model version source

Aliases: CVE-2026-116690

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • mlflow — fixed in 3.17.0

### Summary On MLflow tracking servers running without authentication, which is the default for mlflow server, a remote attacker can read arbitrary files from the server’s filesystem by creating a model version tagged as a prompt whose source is a schemeless local path. The fix for CVE-2026-2614 in 3.10.0 added a prompt-specific branch to the `CreateModelVersion` handler that rejects `file://` URIs and absolute paths but runs path validation only when the source carries a URL scheme. A schemeless value such as `../../etc`, a plain relative name, `.`, a percent-encoded path, or a Windows drive-letter path is therefore stored unchanged as the model version’s artifact location, and the `model-versions/get-artifact endpoint` later serves files from it with the privileges of the server process…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-j7qq-vr8c-xvw3: MLflow CrewAI autologging records LLM provider API keys in logged trace spans
entry.content:
MLflow CrewAI autologging records LLM provider API keys in logged trace spans

Aliases: CVE-2026-116691

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • mlflow — fixed in 3.17.0

### Summary `mlflow.crewai.autolog()` leaks CrewAI LLM provider API keys into MLflow trace telemetry. When a CrewAI `Agent` is instrumented with MLflow autologging, MLflow serializes the agent's `__dict__` and converts its fields to strings. The `llm` field contains the CrewAI LLM object, whose string representation includes its `api_key` in plaintext. As a result, an application that calls `mlflow.crewai.autolog()` can unintentionally send its LLM provider API key to the MLflow trace backend or configured OTLP destination. The application does not need to explicitly log the credential or place it in a span attribute. The credential is extracted automatically by MLflow's instrumentation. This was verified on **MLflow 3.16.0** with **CrewAI 1.15.18** using MLflow's own OTLP exporter. T…

Affected:

  • pillow — fixed in 13.0.0

Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's P;2L and P;4L raw decoders can read past the end of an input buffer. ImagingRawDecode calculates a packed-pixel row size, while the unpackers read separately padded bit planes. A caller can supply a buffer and image dimensions whose accepted size is smaller than the unpacker's actual footprint. This can disclose up to three adjacent heap bytes in output pixels or crash the process. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.
